attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: The proposition and its antecedent are kept. But the drafter mapped 'I expect' to 'likely'. Under policy, unqualified 'I expect' is a scored forecast, not a hedge, so the modality should be 'will'.

contract.note: The contract fairly notes that 'tumble', 'first' and 'far worse' have no measure or deadline. The result depends on whether this is read as stocks or as business. Requiring an Nvidia-first downturn before scoring is faithful to the conditional.

evidence.note: Reuters report on the Jan 2025 DeepSeek one-day selloff, led by Nvidia (-17%) with Microsoft and Alphabet down less. One trading day neither establishes the antecedent nor shows a later, worse outcome for the cloud giants.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm conditional forecast ('I expect'), so it can be scored. Nothing in the packet shows the antecedent, an established Nvidia-first downturn, has happened; one selloff day falls short of that. With no deadline and an unknown antecedent, the evidence cannot settle it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The first-person 'I am seeing' framing and the target, actual adoption, are preserved. The surrounding text uses AI broadly, not only generative AI.

contract.note: Plain reading: thin evidence that businesses had really adopted AI by early 2024. That is an ordinary reading and backed by the surveys he cites. The contract rightly separates limited adoption from no documented deployments.

evidence.note: Census BTOS, nationally weighted, Feb 2024: about 5.4% of firms used AI in production. This is representative evidence of limited deployed use within the target period.
Klarna's own disclosure of a substantial generative-AI deployment. It is a single company, self-reported, and does not show broad adoption.

reviews.rationale: In Q1 2024 the representative Census survey shows only about 5% of firms using AI in production, which fits his plain claim that actual adoption was thin. Klarna is a real deployment but a single self-reported case, so it does not show substantial adoption across businesses.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. The Times lawsuit is background, not his claim.

semantics.note: This is a confident claim about past training. The drafter's 'likely' modality conflicts with policy, which treats 'I'd bet' as a firm, scored commitment. The proposition text itself is faithful.

contract.note: Requiring proof of training on at least two Springer titles before the post, and separating training from licensing or retrieval, is fair. The breadth of the web wording is read ordinarily.

evidence.note: OpenAI's Dec 2023 partnership announcement gives forward-looking training rights. It does not show that Springer content was used in training already completed.
OpenAI states its fair-use position on public web data. It gives no provenance for any specific publication.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm claim ('I'd bet money') about past training, so it can be scored. The packet has no training records, litigation evidence or extraction studies linking Springer titles to a ChatGPT training run before April 2024. Nothing contradicts it either, so it is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. They imply that he now asserts an AI bubble.

semantics.note: The 'hesitant until I read' framing implies a present assertion that we are in an AI bubble. The normalisation captures that core commitment.

contract.note: Plain reading: speculation had pushed AI valuations and investment beyond plausible returns. That is the ordinary meaning of 'bubble', but with no threshold the result turns on interpretation.

evidence.note: RBC, March 2024, calls valuations stretched but not Tech Bubble 2.0. This is a contemporaneous opinion on broad US equities and the Magnificent 7, not a finding about whether AI as a whole was in a bubble.

reviews.rationale: The only item is one analyst's opinion that cuts both ways: valuations stretched, but no dot-com repeat. It covers broad equities rather than AI investment as a whole. Nothing in the packet shows overvaluation across the AI industry in Q1 2024, or that fundamentals justified prices, so the claim is unresolved.
